items.title: Charlie Gabriel interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 9, 2020
items.q: Because Charlie Mingus was in the band at that time.

ctx.x: Did you have to adapt to the rock & roll that came on to the scene, because the tenor players always got the —

That was a natural for me because when I played “Flying Home” with Lionel Hampton that’s one of the things that got me into that band. Because Charlie Mingus was in the band at that time. You know? So I’d play the horn and, you know, I mean you’d go all out to entertain the public. I can’t stand there just blowing my horn you know and look cute you know? You have to move, entertain people. It’s two types of ways of playing. Like I have to tell these guys at the club here right now, when you’re playing jazz, like…
Good advice. Did your father talk about those kinds of things like beyond how good you play the saxophone or the clarinet, you have to behave like this. Did he give you advice?
